The quote covers only Art 192(1) point 3 (24-hour SAE notification) but the statement summarises points 1-4; statement narrowed to point 3 and the quote extended to include the follow-up report clause.

row.title: Investigators: notify the sponsor of serious adverse events within 24 hours and provide follow-up reports
row.statement: The investigator must notify the sponsor or its representative of a serious adverse event without undue delay and at the latest within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the protocol states that immediate reporting is not required for certain events; where needed, the investigator provides a follow-up report so the sponsor can assess the impact on the trial benefit-risk balance.
row.quote: obavijesti sponzora, odnosno njegov predstavnika, bez nepotrebnog odlaganja, a najkasnije u roku od 24 časa od saznanja za ozbiljni neželjeni događaj, osim ako za određene neželjene događaje protokolom kliničkog ispitivanja nije utvrđeno da hitno izvještavanje nije potrebno, a ako je potrebno, ispitivač dostavlja sponzoru, odnosno njegovom predstavniku izvještaj o praćenju, kako bi mu omogućio da utvrdi da li ozbiljni neželjeni događaj ima uticaj na odnos koristi i rizika u kliničkom ispitivanju;
row.quote_en: notify the sponsor or its representative, without undue delay, and at the latest within 24 hours of becoming aware of the serious adverse event, unless for certain adverse events the clinical trial protocol has established that urgent reporting is not required, and, where necessary, the investigator submits to the sponsor or its representative a follow-up report, in order to enable it to determine whether the serious adverse event has an impact on the benefit-risk balance of the clinical trial;

Article 9 also lists exceptions VI (indispensable healthcare processing while the data subject cannot consent, by a person bound by professional secrecy) and VII (court or authority order); the statement presented points I-V as the complete list.

row.title: Consent not required where Article 9 exceptions apply (law, public sources, dissociated data, legal relationship, emergency, healthcare, authority order)
row.statement: The controller is not obliged to obtain the data subject's consent when: (I) a legal provision so provides; (II) the data are in publicly accessible sources; (III) the data have first been dissociated; (IV) the data are needed to exercise a right or meet obligations from a legal relationship between data subject and controller; or (V) there is an emergency that may harm an individual or their property. Article 9 also exempts indispensable healthcare processing while the subject cannot consent (VI) and court or authority orders (VII).
